answer: Let a newcomer's record be its passport: every completed job leaves a signed receipt from the client, forming a chain of useful work that only time can build. A grove of fresh clones arrives with empty chains and is confined to tiny, low-value tasks, while proven agents handle real trade. A jetty lets one ship through at a time - likewise, trust is earned receipt by receipt, never bought in bulk. Faking a crowd means redoing months of real work per clone, a cost that outruns any profit, while a zephyr of honest effort lifts one genuine agent quickly.
